authorizer: Edge: CloudFront EVTSA9VEHNZVH behavior /api/scoped/investor-reporting/* -> APIGateway-portal, viewer-request Lambda@Edge auth-validator-edge:22 (verifies the human JWT, injects the X-User-* headers; its only investor-reporting-specific branch is the RENDER-token branch, which admits four GET routes and not the export routes), WAF opal-cloudfront-protection with no path rule (block-IP, two rate limits, three managed groups in COUNT). Gateway: authorizer naqxlm portal-jwt-authorizer (REQUEST, payload 2.0, simple responses, identity source $request.header.Authorization, result TTL unset) = Lambda opal-portal-authorizer. WHAT IT ADMITS: any request that passes the origin gate and carries a valid RS256 human JWT (issuer opal-portal-auth, audience opal-portal-api), of ANY tier, role, firm or userType; it computes allowedFirmIds for context and does not gate on it. A render-audience token is admitted only on the four RENDER_ROUTE_CLAIMS GETs, never the export routes. The decision that matters is therefore made inside irpt-export-render: firm binding (IRPT_DIRECTORY_BUCKET_MAP carries 49financial, cottonwood, inflection), principal class, non-empty permitted set, then _covered.

fail_open_bearing: The fail-open branch (_covered returns True when the receipt names no account) widens a LIMITED-grant caller only. For the 6 49financial FIRM_ADVISOR principals it means a same-firm export id whose receipt carries no account list reads as covered although the advisor's own permitted set does not contain the export's accounts. For the 1 cottonwood FIRM_OPERATIONS principal the permitted set is the whole firm, so the branch widens nothing beyond the firm. Cross-firm reach is not opened by the branch: the receipt key is built from the verified firm, never the request. Whether any receipt actually names no account was not read (evidence bucket receipts not enumerated).
api_direct_callable: YES. The page gate (App.tsx: requireAdmin, requireInternal, requireDev) is a client-side route guard in the SPA; it hides the page and enforces nothing on the API. No server layer in front of the export routes checks tier, role or firm for a human token: the edge validator has no investor-reporting human-path gate in its source, the WAF has no path rule, and the gateway authorizer admits any valid human JWT. A non-Opal principal with a valid login (the 7 listed) can send GET /api/scoped/investor-reporting/export/{exportId} (and /download) with its own bearer token to the CloudFront host and be served by irpt-export-render. The 23 non-Opal principals not listed reach the function and are refused inside it. Reaching a receipt additionally needs an export id that exists under the principal's own firm.

The class and the permitted set come from running the production classify_principal/resolve/advisor_grant code over reconstructed headers. The JWT claims are assumed to be minted as auth-handler/src/jwt.ts and auth.ts read at this worktree (advisorId = partner advisorKey, advisorRole and firmRole from the partner row); the deployed auth-handler and edge-validator bytes were not diffed to the repo.

NOT READ: lastLogin or MFA state (a principal who never logs in still counts as able to); whether any export receipt exists without an account list; export id guessability; the deployed edge validator version 22 source; the authorizer result cache behaviour (TTL unset in the route config).

JOIN: a profile row is joined to its partner row by email (the key getPartnerIdentity uses); the four partner tables were scanned in full (23 rows). A profile with no partner row classifies as it would at login: no advisorId, so only role=admin reaches a scope.
Opaque ids: p-<10 hex> of sha256 over a random per-run salt that was discarded; no email, name, advisor key or raw account number is in this file.
Opal count (22) counts every opal-capital profile and every userType Dev profile, active or not; reach for them is not graded here by design.
